# Logic and Conditions

Arithmetic, comparisons, logic, and the operators that choose between values or say whether there is one. The
rules for missing values are in [Missing Values](../missing-values.md); precedence is in
[Syntax](../syntax.md#precedence).

## Operators

| Operator | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` | Arithmetic, element by element |
| `**` | Power, with a number as the exponent |
| `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=` | 1 or 0, missing where either side is missing |
| `&`, <code>&#124;</code>, `~` | And, or, not, three-valued |

### Comparisons

A comparison gives 1 or 0, and no value where either side has none: there are no returns on Jan 02.

`returns(1)`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | · | · | · | · |
| Jan 03 | 0.100 | −0.050 | 0.017 | 0.050 |
| Jan 04 | 0.091 | −0.053 | · | −0.024 |
| Jan 05 | −0.083 | 0.028 | 0.016 | 0.049 |
| Jan 08 | 0.182 | −0.081 | 0.032 | 0.023 |
| Jan 09 | 0.077 | −0.059 | −0.016 | 0.045 |

Result: `returns(1) > 0`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | · | · | · | · |
| Jan 03 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 04 | 1 | 0 | · | 0 |
| Jan 05 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 08 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 09 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

### And, or, not

Three-valued: false `&` missing is 0, true `|` missing is 1, and otherwise missing with missing is missing. Below,
"up today and high-beta". On Jan 02 there are no returns: **B** and **D** have betas under 1, so the answer is 0
without knowing the return; for **A** and **C** it depends on the return, so there is no answer.

`returns(1) > 0`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | · | · | · | · |
| Jan 03 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 04 | 1 | 0 | · | 0 |
| Jan 05 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 08 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 09 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

`field('beta') > 1`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 03 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 04 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 05 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 08 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 09 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |

Result: `(returns(1) > 0) & (field('beta') > 1)`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | · | 0 | · | 0 |
| Jan 03 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 04 | 1 | 0 | · | 0 |
| Jan 05 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 08 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 09 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

`&` and `|` bind tighter than comparisons, so the parentheses are needed.

## Choosing values

### where

<p class="sig"><code>where(cond, if_true, if_false)</code></p>

`if_true` where `cond` is nonzero, `if_false` where it is 0, and no value where it is missing.

Below, the day's return rank, for high-beta stocks only.

`field('beta') > 1`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 03 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 04 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 05 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 08 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Jan 09 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |

Result: `where(field('beta') > 1, rank(returns(1)), None)`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | · | · | · | · |
| Jan 03 | 1.00 | · | 0.50 | · |
| Jan 04 | 1.00 | · | · | · |
| Jan 05 | 0.25 | · | 0.50 | · |
| Jan 08 | 1.00 | · | 0.75 | · |
| Jan 09 | 1.00 | · | 0.50 | · |

```qex
where(volatility(20) > 0.6, None, rank(-returns(5)))      # leave out the most volatile stocks
```

### coalesce

<p class="sig"><code>coalesce(x, y)</code></p>

`x` where it has a value, else `y`: a number, a label or an expression. It says what missing should mean: below, a
day without a report counts as no surprise. Choose with care: a missing return is not a 0% return.

`field('surprise')`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | · | · | · | · |
| Jan 03 | 0.05 | · | · | · |
| Jan 04 | · | · | · | · |
| Jan 05 | · | · | −0.02 | · |
| Jan 08 | · | −0.01 | · | 0.03 |
| Jan 09 | · | · | · | · |

Result: `coalesce(field('surprise'), 0)`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Jan 03 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Jan 04 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Jan 05 | 0.00 | 0.00 | −0.02 | 0.00 |
| Jan 08 | 0.00 | −0.01 | 0.00 | 0.03 |
| Jan 09 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |

```qex
coalesce(field('price') > 5, 0)              # no price counts as not above $5
coalesce(group('sector'), 'Other')           # a label for stocks without one
```

### None

<p class="sig"><code>None</code></p>

No value here, on purpose: `where(cond, x, None)`. `None` and `0` are different answers. A `0` is a value, and once
a book demeans the signal it is a position against the day's average; `None` takes the stock out.

## Is there a value?

### is_valid

<p class="sig"><code>is_valid(x)</code></p>

1 where `x` has a value, else 0. An infinity counts as a value.

`close()`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | 10.0 | 20.0 | 30.0 | 40.0 |
| Jan 03 | 11.0 | 19.0 | 30.5 | 42.0 |
| Jan 04 | 12.0 | 18.0 | · | 41.0 |
| Jan 05 | 11.0 | 18.5 | 31.0 | 43.0 |
| Jan 08 | 13.0 | 17.0 | 32.0 | 44.0 |
| Jan 09 | 14.0 | 16.0 | 31.5 | 46.0 |

Result: `is_valid(close())`

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 02 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 03 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 04 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Jan 05 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 08 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jan 09 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

```qex
is_valid(field('surprise'))                  # 1 on report days
```

### is_finite

<p class="sig"><code>is_finite(x)</code></p>

1 where `x` is a finite number, 0 where it is missing or infinite.

```qex
where(is_finite(volume(20) / volume(1)), volume(20) / volume(1), None)
```
